n: From inside the fish, Jonah finally prays. Note “his God” — Jonah turns back to the God he tried to escape.
Jonah’s prayer is a psalm of thanksgiving. Even from what felt like the depths of death, he called and God heard him.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol — the realm of the dead; Jonah felt as good as dead.

f.w: I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me

n: Jonah recognizes God’s hand: though the sailors threw him, it was the Lord who cast him into the deep. Waves and currents swept over him.

f.w: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me

n: Feeling banished from God’s presence, Jonah still resolves to look toward the temple — a sign of renewed faith.

f.w: I am cast out of thy sight

n: The water rose to his throat, the deep surrounded him, and seaweed wrapped around his head — a vivid picture of drowning.

f.g: Up to the neck or throat — to the point of death.

n: He sank to the roots of the mountains, locked in as if by the bars of death’s prison — yet God brought him up from the pit. The low point becomes a turning point.

f.g: The underworld pictured as a city with gates barred shut.

n: When his life was ebbing away, Jonah remembered the Lord, and his prayer reached God’s holy temple.

f.w: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD

n: Those who cling to worthless idols abandon the loyal love God offers them. Ironically, the idol-worshiping sailors had just turned to God.

f.g: Give up the steadfast love (Hebrew ḥesed) that could be theirs.

n: Jonah vows to give thanks and keep his promises. “Salvation is of the Lord” — the theme of the whole book.

f.w: I will pay that that I have vowed

n: The Lord speaks, and the fish spits Jonah out onto dry land. Even the creatures obey God more readily than His prophet had.

f.g: Cast out — an earthy, almost comic picture.
